newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: China to open new instant coffee plant in weeks.
newsitem.headline: China to open new instant coffee plant in weeks.

text.p: China will open a new instant coffee plant in the next few weeks, a leading Indonesian coffee consultant said here Wednesday.

Derek Watson, a coffee veteran of 40 years and consultant to the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters, said the opening would come on top of the three major instant coffee plants already found in China.

Watson did not say which company was behind the new plant, but added both Switzerland's Nestle and General Foods already had coffee operations in the country. Watson is in Costa Rica for the International Coffee Week, known in Spanish as Sintercafe.
China is the great future hope for the coffee industry since its massive population largely shuns for other favourites drinks, such as tea.

Watson said the International Coffee Organisation (ICO), the London based coffee institution that has a role in compiling industry statistics, will use funds to campaign for greater coffee consumption in China and also in Russia, the two countries the industry believes has most potential for rapid growth.
"I don't want to mention a figure for the estimated consumption these two countries could reach because it would frighten people," he added.

Watson said the promotional campaign needed to get off the ground. "The campaign, which I would like to see supported by industry, could be the catalyst (to boost coffee consumption in China and Russia)," he added.
